subject: Follow-up: Long-context evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmehealth.com>, Jill Torres <jill.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up from this morning \u0014 long-context evals & next steps

Hi Samir / Jill \u0014

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

What we heard:
- Primary goal: accurate extraction and summarization from multi-document medical notes (~20\u001340k tokens per patient record).
- Key constraints: strict PII handling, predictable tail latency for <300ms per token for interactive use, and no lossy truncation for the most important sections.
- Success metrics: ROUGE/QA pass rates on your clinical QA prompt set, and no more than 2% summary hallucination on a 1k-sample baseline.

What we propose now:
1) Run our long-context eval using your prompt set (you shared sample prompts) against three model/config buckets:
   - redwood-lite-13b-8k (fast, lower cost)
   - redwood-64b-32k (balanced accuracy, 32k context)
   - redwood-70b-65k (best fidelity for very long context; higher cost)
2) Evaluate truncation behavior and summarization fidelity using the ACME prompt set (attached). We'll produce per-prompt regression metrics and per-token latency histograms.
3) Pilot timeline: 2 weeks for full eval run + a 1-week review sync.

Attachments and links: prompt set (attached: acme_long_context_prompt_set.md), evaluation dashboard (link below), and a short note on recommended configs.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm the sample prompt set attached is the canonical one we should run.
- Share any restricted samples (redacted) for PII verification; if needed we can run in your Private deployment.
- Are you ok with the proposed pilot scope (2\u00133 model variants + truncation/summarization checks)?

I'll loop Dev on the technical details (kv-cache, prefix caching, eval infra) \u0014 he added some notes below.

Thanks \u0014
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa \u0014 thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying q's: 

1) For the 65k context model, can you confirm whether that is a contiguous context window or whether it supports multi-file indexing with semantic search + on-the-fly retrieval? We care because many records are split across documents.
2) What does your truncation policy look like if the summary prompt exceeds the model window? Do you do intelligent fallback (head/tail prioritization) or hard truncation?
3) On cost \u0014 can you give a rough ballpark for the eval run vs what a sustained Dedicated deployment might look like (per 1M tokens/day)?

Also attaching a sample redacted clinical note that represents a worst-case length. Please treat as confidential.

Samir
Head of Data Integration | Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_sample_redacted_note.txt (text/plain)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from this morning \u0014 long-context evals & next steps

Samir \u0014 quick technical answers to your questions: 

1) 65k window: the "redwood-70b-65k" variant supports a contiguous 65k token autoregressive window for a single request. For multi-file records we recommend a hybrid approach: semantic retrieval to bring in relevant documents (cheap) + large-window model for final summarization. That gives the best cost/accuracy tradeoff.

2) Truncation behavior: our runtime defaults to head-prioritization (keeps the beginning of the sequence) but for summarization we can use a custom windowing policy that preserves user-specified anchors (e.g., "Preserve: Findings section until summary step"). We also support iterative chunking + stitching mode which reduces hallucination in very long documents.

3) Cost: rough ballparks (hosted API, standard q4 quantized runtimes, per-token):
   - redwood-lite-13b-8k: $0.0008 / 1k tokens (inference only)
   - redwood-64b-32k: $0.0035 / 1k tokens
   - redwood-70b-65k: $0.009 / 1k tokens
For a 1M tokens/day sustained Dedicated commit we'd provide a discounted egress + reserved GPU pricing \u0014 I'll have finance give exact numbers once we lock expected throughput.

Attached: preliminary eval run we did on a small subset (long_context_eval_results.csv) so you get a sense of truncation/fidelity tradeoffs. Key notes: iterative chunk+stitch reduces hallucination by ~60% vs single-pass on the worst-case notes; 65k model gave the best end-to-end QA pass rate but at ~2.8x the per-token cost of the 32k variant.

-Dev
Staff SWE, Inference
[Attachment: long_context_eval_results.csv (text/csv)]
